thoughts: Monday morning and the shop's still on my mind. Last month's figures wobbled badly — one week we lost 171 baskets because the shelves were bare, and I've still got 24 units spoiling in a fortnight. I need stock in without tying up money I don't have. The Calder paperwork's a mess: Sian says one retainer at $30 a week for seven weeks, nothing beyond, but there are four overlapping entries sitting there. I'll keep the seven-week one and cancel the duplicates so nobody's paid twice. And I'm not signing a thing with Owen's loan in it until the interest rate and full repayment are written out plain — I don't owe what I can't see. Keith's chasing those four Thursday slots and the letter's in that drawer somewhere; I'll get him to bring it into the shop so I can read it myself. Alan's booked for Tuesday, so I want the rent figures in front of me before I walk in there. Household's got the energy bill and the loan payment to clear, so let's get those paid and stop worrying about them. Gary Tully's asking for work — I like him, but with the shop account tight I can't take on another wage just now.
aims: Keep one Calder retainer: $30/week for seven weeks
Get Owen's loan terms written out plainly before signing
Find Keith's hospital letter and four Thursday slots
Prepare for Alan's rent talk on Tuesday
Stock shelves without tying up shop cash
